content:
Requirement R18 (input): Set Tracking Distance from TOI. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to set the standoff/tracking distance from the target..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-18.1, F-18.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-18.<F>.1, Be-18.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-18.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** Let the pilot set the standoff/tracking distance from an already-tracked TOI (UAV maintains that range), using Touch and Keyboard.

**Function candidates:**

**F-18.1 — Specify a numeric standoff distance to the tracked TOI.**
Goal: the pilot inputs a discrete distance value (e.g. 2.0 NM) that becomes the UAV's commanded range from the target. Distance-as-a-value, entered and committed.

**F-18.2 — Adjust the UAV's standoff distance relative to its current range.**
Goal: the pilot increments/decrements the current standoff from where it is, rather than typing an absolute figure — a "closer / farther" trim goal. Different interaction goal: relative correction under time pressure, not authoring an absolute number.

**F-18.3 — Set standoff distance by spatial designation against the tracked geometry.**
Goal: the pilot expresses the desired range geometrically (e.g. placing a ring/point relative to the TOI on the map/feed) and the system derives the distance. Goal is spatial-visual specification rather than numeric entry.

Note on scope: F-18.3 overlaps conceptually with R14/R17 map-designation structures and could reuse them — flagging now since it's relevant. But it changes the *unit of intent* from a distance to a position, which arguably drifts from R18's stated "set distance" intent. F-18.1 is the closest literal match to the use case (7.2.1 "defines a new tracking distance"); F-18.2 adds genuine operational value for high-workload trim.

Which function do you want to close on?
1, but the structure can also display the current range so the user can make relative adjustments easily.

**F-18.1 closed** — Specify a numeric standoff distance to the tracked TOI. The panel will surface the *current* commanded/actual range as context, so absolute entry doubles as an informed relative adjustment (no separate increment function — the displayed current value is what enables easy trimming).

**Behaviour candidates (F=18.1):**

**Be-18.1.1 — Keyboard-only:** Current range shown as a live readout. Pilot enters a new distance value via UCP alphanumeric keypad (or bezel rotary to step the value up/down from the displayed current). Envelope validation (min/max standoff) gates a CONFIRM before the command is sent. Rotary-stepping-from-current is what makes relative trim effortless without a separate function.

**Be-18.1.2 — Touch-only:** Current range shown as a live readout. Pilot taps a distance field to raise an on-screen numeric keypad, or uses touch +/− stepper buttons anchored to the current value; taps CONFIRM. Stepper increments give the same trim-from-current ease via Touch.

**Be-18.1.3 — Mixed:** Interleaved — e.g. touch to select the field, keyboard/rotary to enter/step the value, either modality to CONFIRM. Adds value: matches R01/R11 multi-input pattern, lets the pilot start on one modality and commit on another mid-task (hands-on-throttle contingency).

All three share one validation gate and one confirm semantics. Note: this is structurally the same multi-input+validate+confirm pattern as R11 (UAV PARAMS) — the Behaviour is effectively a reuse of that pathway applied to a distance value. Flagging for consolidation.

Which pathway(s) to carry into Structure?

All three carried forward. Structures below cover the Keyboard, Touch, and Mixed pathways with shared elements.

**Structure candidates (F=18.1, Be=all three):**

**S-18.1.*.1 — Field embedded in the R17 TOI panel.**
Add a DISTANCE row to the existing R17 unified TOI panel (the same panel that already holds designation + contact list for the tracked target). Elements:
- Current-range live readout (Screen/WAD) — commanded value + actual value.
- Editable distance field: touch-tap raises on-screen numeric keypad (Be-18.1.2); UCP keypad / bezel rotary steps or types (Be-18.1.1); interleaved (Be-18.1.3).
- Touch +/− steppers and rotary both bound to step-from-current.
- Shared envelope-validation gate → reuses R17's dual-input CONFIRM gate.
Rationale: distance is an attribute *of the tracked target*, so it lives with the track command. Tightest coupling, no new panel, one confirm semantics with R17.

**S-18.1.*.2 — Cloned parametric panel (R11-style), standalone.**
A separate docked DISTANCE panel cloned from R11's UAV PARAMS layout, own state. Same multi-input field + current-range readout + validation + CONFIRM, but concurrently displayable alongside PARAMS/status/ISR panes.
Rationale: consistent with the R11/R12/R16 clone family; independent of R17's panel real-estate. Cost: a distinct surface for one value, and distance detaches from the track command visually.

**S-18.1.*.3 — Map/feed ring overlay + numeric field hybrid.**
Current-range shown as a standoff ring around the TOI on map/feed; the same numeric field (touch keypad + keyboard/rotary) drives it, ring redraws live; CONFIRM commits.
Rationale: gives spatial context for the numeric value (borrows F-18.3's idea as *display only*, not as the input goal). Cost: heavier; the ring is visualization, and input still resolves through the numeric field — verify it doesn't reintroduce spatial designation we dropped.

Recommendation: **S-18.1.*.1** — distance belongs on the R17 track command, reuses its confirm gate, minimal new structure. S-18.1.*.3's ring can be layered onto S-18.1.*.1 later as an optional readout if desired.

Which structure?
1 is fine, as long as this distance is editable while tracking without needing to "re-track" again every time the user needs to change the distance from the TOI

**Confirmed — S-18.1.\*.1**, with the explicit constraint: the DISTANCE row is **independently editable and committable while a track is active**. Editing/confirming distance issues a standalone distance-update command (mapping to UC 7.2.2–7.2.4) and does **not** re-trigger R17's track-command gate or re-designate the TOI. Two separate commit paths on the shared panel:
- R17 CONFIRM → track/designation command.
- R18 distance CONFIRM → distance-only update against the already-tracked TOI.

Distance field stays live and re-editable for the duration of the track; current-range readout updates continuously.

**Final for R18:**
- **F-18.1** — Specify a numeric standoff distance to the tracked TOI (current range displayed as context for informed relative adjustment).
- **Be-18.1.1 / .2 / .3** — Keyboard-only, Touch-only, Mixed pathways; shared envelope-validation + confirm; rotary/stepper step-from-current for effortless trim.
- **S-18.1.\*.1** — DISTANCE row embedded in the R17 TOI panel: current+actual range readout, multi-input editable field (touch keypad / UCP / rotary / steppers), independent distance-only confirm gate that operates live during tracking without re-tracking.

Reuse flags for consolidation: multi-input+validate+confirm pattern shared with R11/R17; hosted on R17's panel.

Ready to close R18, or anything to adjust?
